newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex gives new Campeche offshore reserves data.
newsitem.headline: Pemex gives new Campeche offshore reserves data.

text.p: Mexican state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) gave new reserves data for its Campeche Sound offshore production area Monday.

The Campeche offshore region's proven reserves as of January 1, 1997 were 17.1 billion barrels of crude oil equivalent -- 14.64 billion in the northeast marine region and 2.47 billion in the southwest marine region, Pemex said.
The current net value of those proven reserves was almost $140 billion, it said.

Original in situ total volume in the Campeche Sound was 74 billion bbl of crude equivalent, Pemex said in the report, compiled over the last year according to international standards and audited by Netherland, Sewell & Associates Inc.
New reserves data for Pemex's South and North production regions would be published in 1998 and 1999, respectively.

Pemex said its Cantarell complex in the northeast offshore region had proven reserves of 12.33 billion bbl of crude equivalent, was one of the world's few super-giant fields and was "still in an early phase of its development" after 18 years of production.
Renovation of the Cantarell complex's infrastructure was beginning this year and secondary drilling using injection of natural gas and nitrogen would also begin at the same time, it added.
